candidates.name: Tina Kotek
candidates.linkBasis: ORESTAR Statement of Organization for committee 4792 lists candidate Tina Kotek and the office of Governor for the 2026 general election. The committee has been registered for the office of Governor since September 2021.

candidates.name: Christine Drazan
candidates.linkBasis: ORESTAR Statement of Organization for committee 19050 lists candidate Christine Drazan and the office of Governor for the 2026 general election. The committee was registered for State Representative, 51st District, until October 27, 2025, when it was amended to Governor.

candidates.name: Brett Smith
candidates.linkBasis: No committee naming Brett Smith appears among the filers with transactions in this snapshot. Under ORS 260.043 a candidate who expects to raise and spend no more than $750 in a calendar year does not have to form a committee or file transactions, so the absence of records is missing coverage and does not show that he raised nothing.

sourceKinds.note: Committees and organizations that gave $50,000 or more to either candidate, grouped by sponsor where the sponsor is clear from the name, from the committee's own filings in this snapshot, or from the cited source. Everything else keeps the contributor type on the filing.

limits.basis: ORS 260 as amended by chapter 9, Oregon Laws 2024 (HB 4024) and chapter 139, Oregon Laws 2026 (HB 4018): a candidate for governor may not accept more than $3,300 per election from a person. The law defines a person to include individuals, corporations, limited liability companies and labor organizations. The primary and general are separate elections.

filingDeadlines.basis: ORS 260.057: transactions are due within 30 calendar days, or within seven calendar days during the 42 days before an election. Transactions from before that window that are still unfiled are due by the 35th day before the election.

laterBalances.basis: OPB reported on October 1, 2026 that the governor had $4.4 million on hand as of that afternoon and Drazan roughly $1.6 million.

tenMillion.basis: The North Coast States Regional Council of Carpenters gave $10 million to its Oregon committee, Building a Stronger Oregon, on September 16, 2026. The union's director of government relations told OPB the money is for several candidates and measures going forward and is not aimed at one race this year.
tenMillion.quote: is to support multiple candidates and multiple measures from today moving forward
tenMillion.speaker: Ron Rowlett, director of government relations for the carpenters union

primary.basis: May 19, 2026 primary: Drazan won the Republican nomination with 41% over Ed Diehl (31%) and Chris Dudley (16%); Kotek won the Democratic nomination with 84%.
